biophysical_burden.boundary: Annual global burden estimate, not current acceleration, net soil balance, remaining soil depth or a country panel.

human_economic_burden.boundary: Source-attributed agricultural production loss; no broader land-degradation cost is added.

persistence.boundary: The source reports an annual recurring global burden; no multi-year trend is inferred.

extent.boundary: Global arable-land aggregate, not uniform local erosion.

source_snapshot.source_locator: FAO newsroom statement: globally 75 billion tonnes of soil are lost from arable land each year and an estimated US$400 billion in agricultural production is lost.

transformations.formula: Normalize the FAO global annual arable-soil loss estimate through named mass ranges.
Normalize only the FAO agricultural-production-loss estimate; exclude broader land-degradation costs.
365 recurring days / 365 calendar days; do not infer a current acceleration rate.
Score the source-declared global arable-land scope while retaining spatial heterogeneity.

receipts.uncertainty: The summary provides point estimates without observation-level uncertainty. Global aggregation combines heterogeneous climates, soils, land uses and methods; erosion, deposition and soil formation vary. Agricultural-production loss depends on valuation and attribution assumptions.
receipts.freshness: FAO Global Soil Partnership global burden statement 2017; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T19:09:58.309Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: FAO quantifies a recurring global annual arable-soil burden and associated agricultural-production loss, providing biophysical, economic, recurrence and global-extent evidence.
higher_priority_failures: The existing SoilGrids snapshot estimates soil properties, not erosion flux.
No source-consistent current 20-year annual or 60-month global erosion-rate panel supplies magnitude plus threshold or momentum, so the annual burden is not mislabeled current data.
